ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Cars A and B travel in the same direction on a straight and level road. During the time from t=0 to t=t1, their v-t graphs are as shown in the figure. During this time interval, which car has the greater average speed?
ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_answer: The average speed of car A is greater than that of B
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure is a v-t graph, with the vertical axis being speed v and the horizontal axis being time t, and the comparison interval being from 0 to t1. Car A's curve gradually rises from v1 on the left side, and approaches/reaches v2 at t1; Car B's curve gradually decreases from v2 on the left side, and approaches/reaches v1 at t1. The two curves intersect in the earlier segment: at the beginning B is above A, and after the intersection point A is above B; looking at the figure as a whole, the total area under A's curve from 0 to t1 is greater than the total area under B's curve. Reasoning: The area enclosed by a v-t graph and the time axis represents displacement. The problem states that the two cars travel in the same direction, and what is compared is the same time interval from 0 to t1, therefore average speed = displacement/time; with the same time, whichever has the greater displacement has the greater average speed. Since the area under Car A's v-t curve is greater, Car A's displacement is greater, so Car A's average speed is greater.
